Article Title: Delimitation row: CM Vijay moves resolution to freeze Lok Sabha Seats at 543
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu assembly backs 543 Lok Sabha seat freeze

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday moved a special resolution in the state Assembly urging the Centre to permanently retain the Lok Sabha’s strength at 543 seats.Days after convening a meeting of parties supporting his government, including the Congress and the Left parties that extend support from outside, Vijay moved the resolution in the Assembly urging the Centre to maintain the Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha seat ratio at 2.2:1.The government-sponsored resolution urged the Centre to implement 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections without delay, based on the existing strength of 543 seats."The 33% reservation for women should be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections itself, based on the existing 543 constituencies. The 33% reservation for women should not be delayed any further. In Tamil Nadu, more women have voted than men. Providing reservation for women is not a concession; it is a matter of social justice. The 33% reservation for women must be implemented without any further delay," Vijay said in the assembly.The resolution noted that the population of states, including Tamil Nadu, and the Union Territories has not been counted for more than five decades, with the next census scheduled for 2026."All the states including Tamil Nadu and the people / elected representatives of the union territories have not had their population counted for more than 50 years.The next census to count the population was supposed to be held in 2026. Therefore, since the delimitation of constituencies has not been carried out for the last 50 years, based on the 2011 population census, the constituencies should be delimited and the number of Lok Sabha and Assembly members should be increased from 550 to 850 by bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill," the resolution stated.Last week, a meeting convened by Vijay with Tamil Nadu MPs from alliance and friendly parties decided to oppose the Union government’s proposed delimitation exercise in its entirety.The meeting was boycotted by the main opposition DMK and the AIADMK, with the former calling the deliberations a “farce” and the latter describing them as a “hurriedly staged drama”.The MPs had demanded that the ratio of seats between the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha be maintained at 2.2:1. They also unanimously agreed to adopt a resolution in the state Assembly to permanently safeguard the interests of Tamil Nadu and other southern states in the delimitation process.Meanwhile, the AIADMK called the meeting a “hurriedly staged drama”, pointing out that no fresh delimitation Bill had been introduced in Parliament and that there had been no official announcement on the exercise.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed linking its implementation to the delimitation exercise and have demanded that the two be delinked.The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, was passed by both Houses of Parliament. However, its implementation has not moved forward after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell in the Lok Sabha on April 17, failing to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.The Bill had linked the implementation of 33% reservation for women in legislatures to the delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu assembly backs 543 Lok Sabha seat freeze. Government-sponsored resolution urges Centre to implement 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Meeting boycotted by main opposition DMK and the AIADMK, with former calling deliberations a “farce”

Article Title: 'Generation gutter' remark on NEET protesters: Agra lawyer files case against BJP MP Kangana Ranaut

NEW DELHI: An Agra-based lawyer on Wednesday said he has filed a case against BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut over her remarks describing students who protested against the NEET paper leak as “Generation gutter.”Rajiv Gandhi Bar Association president and advocate Ramashankar Sharma alleged that Ranaut had “insulted” the students and their parents. He also accused the BJP MP of having a “habit” of making such remarks."I have filed a suit in the Special Court for MPs/MLAs. The suit concerns Kangana Ranaut referring to students protesting at Jantar Mantar as the 'gutter generation'. She has a habit of making such remarks. She has insulted the country's students and abused their parents... This is a matter concerning the students' future," Sharma told ANI.The court is scheduled to hear the matter on August 21.The case comes after Ranaut criticised students protesting over the NEET paper leak, describing some of them as “Generation Gutter” and questioning their behaviour and language.In a series of posts on Instagram Stories, the actor-politician described videos from the agitation as “puke-inducing” and criticised the protesters for what she called their “crass” language and behaviour.She also questioned the "upbringing" of the young protesters and criticised some young women for trying to emulate independent career women without “earning that freedom”.Ranaut later wrote that some protesters had “nothing to offer to the system” and were “not good at studies”, referring to them as “Generation Gutter”.The agitation was called off on July 25 after then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. During the agitation, some youngsters allegedly abused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late mother.They were booked after the protests ended, following which PM Modi said he had "forgiven" the alleged abusers.

Article Title: ‘CJP twisted CJI remark’: Supreme Court seeks government, CBI response on PIL
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Three months after CJI Surya Kant's 'cockroach' remark sparked a storm and gave birth to Cockroach Janta Party that led a Gen Z protest against NEET-UG paper leak, Supreme Court Tuesday sought responses from govt and CBI on a PIL seeking action against those who commercially exploited the remark through clever editing of virtual court proceedings and draped it with a meaning that was never intended.During a half-an-hour long debate on the issue before a bench comprising CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, petitioner-cum-advocate Raja Choudhary said it requires a deeper investigation as to how the word 'cockroach', used in a completely different context during judicial proceedings on May 15, was selectively picked, cleverly edited and commercially exploited to undermine judicial dignity and hurt institutional integrity. The petitioner sought a direction to authorities "to examine and take action in accordance with law against persons/entities allegedly involved in commercial exploitation, trademark appropriation, monetized circulation, or unauthorised commercial use of oral courtroom observations/metaphors, including activities of CJP, while recognising that fair criticism, democratic dissent, satire, and free speech remain permissible within the constitutional framework without undermining institutional dignity".Referring to the May 15 hearing before a CJI-led bench on a petition 'Sanjay Dubey Vs Registrar General of Delhi HC', Choudhary emphasised the CJI had made the "cockroach" remark in the specific context of fake advocates, as he expressed "concerns regarding misuse of court process, deterioration of professional standards and how it impacted the institution itself".He said post-May 15, there has been a quantum increase in clips of selectively edited judicial proceedings. The distorted versions and oral observations made during court proceedings are turned into memes and are circulated in social media for profit, said Chaudhary.He complained there is no mechanism against these sinister designs aimed at diminishing public faith in the institution and judges by showing them in poor light.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant's 'cockroach' remark sparked a storm and gave birth to Cockroach Janta Party that led a Gen Z protest against NEET-UG paper leak. Supreme Court sought responses from govt and CBI on a PIL seeking action against those who commercially exploited the remark.

Article Title: ‘Only God can save this country’: HC bins plea of J&K cop sacked for skipping duty over terror threat
Article Text:
"Engagement of SPOs is not of a permanent nature but only to take care of a particular contingency,” the HC noted.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Srinagar: Only God can save this country if a police officer, of whatever rank, gets frightened by terrorists’ threats and refuses duties, J&K high court has said while dismissing a cop’s petition for reinstatement.“The justification provided by the petitioner for not attending his duties is unacceptable, to say the least,” a single bench of Justice Sanjay Dhar said in its Monday order. The judge rejected special police officer (SPO) Hemo Hamid Wani’s argument that he was entitled to the “same powers, privileges and protections available to ordinary officers of police under Police Act”. The HC pointed out that “SPOs do not hold any civil posts regulated by statutory rules”.Residents of a neighbourhood are appointed SPOs “for specific purposes when the force ordinarily employed for preserving peace is not sufficient”. “Thus, engagement of SPOs is not of a permanent nature but only to take care of a particular contingency,” the HC noted.Wani was engaged as an SPO in 2012. In 2015, he was posted at Reshipora in south Kashmir’s Shopian. While at home on medical leave at one point then, he received life threats from terrorists and failed to report back to duties.When he returned after some time to his posting, he was not allowed to join duty, forcing him to take the matter to senior officers.When no action was taken, Wani moved the HC. In Aug last year, the court directed the J&K police DGP to take a decision on Wani’s plea. The DGP turned it down, forcing Wani to move the HC again.In his HC petition, Wani argued that J&K Police had disengaged him without inquiry, formal charges or hearing. The action, he said, violated the Constitution’s Articles 16 (equality of opportunity in public employment), 21 (right to life and livelihood) and 311 (protection against arbitrary dismissal), besides provisions of J&K Police Rules.The HC rejected the contentions, saying Wani, as an SPO, was not entitled to any hearing or inquiry in view of the temporary nature of his engagement. Even if it is assumed that Wani had the right to such a hearing, his failure to perform duties in the face of terror threats is enough reason to remove him, the HC held.“Granting an opportunity to the petitioner to present his case prior to disengagement would have been an empty formality. The DGP has rightly rejected the petitioner’s representation. The order does not call for any interference,” Justice Dhar observed.
Article Summary: J&K high court dismisses a cop's petition for reinstatement. Hemo Hamid Wani was engaged as an SPO in 2012. In 2015, he was posted at Reshipora in south Kashmir’s Shopian. While at home on medical leave, he received life threats from terrorists.

Article Title: Kashmiri Pandits’ security stepped up after ‘threat letter’ from Lashkar arm
Article Text:
IGP Kashmir VK Birdi said the police were probing the threat letter, believed to have been released on social media on Aug 7.

SRINAGAR: J&K police have tightened security in areas of the Valley where Kashmiri Pandits live and allowed some employees to work from home temporarily after Panun Kashmir claimed a purported threat letter from Lashkar affiliate United Liberation Council naming several community members and listing their phone numbers.“Authorities must investigate the source of the information, the digital trail behind the communication and whether any surveillance, profiling or reconnaissance of the targeted persons has taken place,” Agnishekar, convenor of Panun Kashmir said, adding it was important to establish whether the “perpetrators actually possessed the information or were using it as a form of psychological warfare”.IGP Kashmir VK Birdi said the police were probing the threat letter, believed to have been released on social media on Aug 7. Divisional commissioner Anshul Garg said some Pandits had been allowed to work from home, but there was no blanket order. Education officials said the department had not issued any such work-from-home order for all Pandit staff.According to Panun Kashmir’s Agnishekar, “the letter represented a serious escalation as it went beyond generic threats and appeared to identify individuals as potential targets while claiming access to information about their families, locations and places of work”.“The publication of names and personal contact details, accompanied by explicit threats to pursue the individuals and their families, is a matter of grave concern. This is not something that can be dismissed as mere rhetoric. It has the unmistakable potential to intimidate the targeted individuals and terrorise the wider Kashmiri Pandit community,” Agnishekar said.The threat was particularly disturbing in view of the community’s history of being victims of targeted killings, intimidation and forced displacement from Kashmir, Agnishekar pointed out. Jammu-based Panun Kashmir seeks a separate homeland for Pandits in the Valley with Union territory status.Kashmiri Pandit Sangarsh Samiti, another community group representing those who stayed back in the Valley after 1990s’ migration, called the new threat a conspiracy to sabotage their existence. “Recent terror attacks in south Kashmir, followed by fresh threat posters naming Kashmiri Pandit employees, have once again exposed the chilling sense of vulnerability,” KPSS said.In 2008, the Manmohan Singh-led UPA govt introduced a rehabilitation package for the Pandits who had to leave the Valley in the 1990s in the face of terror. Among other measures, the package provided 6,000 govt jobs and created new posts. Such people are posted in various departments across Kashmir and are called “PM package employees”.
Article Summary: J&K police have tightened security in areas of the Valley where Kashmiri Pandits live and allowed some employees to work from home temporarily. Panun Kashmir claimed a purported threat letter from Lashkar affiliate United Liberation Council naming several community members and listing their phone numbers.

Article Title: Assessing implications of Mecca defence pact: India
Article Text:
Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, accompanied by their ministers of Foreign Affairs and Defence, pose after signing a joint defence agreement in Mecca.

NEW DELHI: India continues to examine the implications of the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkiye security pact for its own security as well as regional peace and stability, said ministry of external affairs. The ministry also stressed that India remains fully committed to safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard.The Mecca joint defence agreement may be designed to address West Asia dynamics but it has also led to concerns in India about possible long-term diplomatic and security challenges that it might pose for the country vis-a-vis its relations with Pakistan.The primary concern for now of course is what the pact might mean for its policy of zero tolerance against cross-border terrorism and of setting a strategic deterrence against Pakistan's support for the same, amid the likelihood of an augmentation of Pakistani military capabilities through the agreement."As far as this agreement is concerned, we are examining its implications both from the perspective of India's national security and considerations of regional peace and stability,"said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. TNN
Article Summary: India continues to examine the implications of the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkiye security pact for its own security as well as regional peace and stability. India remains fully committed to safeguarding its national interests and will take all necessary measures in this regard.

Article Title: Border issue will reflect on bilateral ties: Delhi to Beijing
Article Text:
Arunachal is an integral and inalienable part of India, and this is a self-evident fact, MEA said

NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh is indisputably an integral and inalienable part of India, govt asserted Tuesday in response to Beijing’s rejection of its decision to formally identify and map 27 places in the state. Following recent reports about fresh border tensions, govt also reiterated that “the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of larger bilateral ties”.The home ministry had last week identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by “standard place and feature names” on the official maps of Survey of India, saying this would facilitate their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public. China, which has at least on six occasions assigned new names to places in Arunachal to reinforce its claim over the state, called the action “illegal, null and void”.“Arunachal Pradesh is an integral and inalienable part of India, and this is a self-evident fact. Nothing can change this indisputable reality,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, responding to queries about remarks by the Chinese foreign ministry.The Indian exercise had followed unconfirmed reports of incursions by PLA into Arunachal Pradesh. CM Pema Khandu had denied there was any such incursion by Chinese troops.The MEA said India had always emphasised that the maintenance of peace in border areas was of the utmost importance. “We have also stated that the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties,” Jaiswal said, adding this was reiterated at the 36th Meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China border affairs, where the two sides engaged in “frank discussions” and reviewed the situation along LAC.“It was agreed to continue to use existing diplomatic and military channels... to avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along LAC,” the official said.
Article Summary: The home ministry had last week identified 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by “standard place and feature names” on the official maps of Survey of India. China, which has at least on six occasions assigned new names to places in the state, called the action “illegal, null and void”

Article Title: Terror suspects spotted, search operations launched in J&K’s Doda & Poonch
Article Text:
Additional personnel from the Army, CRPF and police, along with reinforcements, were rushed to the area

JAMMU: Security forces launched joint cordon-and-search operations in J&K’s Doda and Poonch districts on being alerted about the sighting of terror suspects, officials said Tuesday.Cordon-and-search operations were initiated in Doda’s upper reaches after some locals captured a video of four suspected ultras trekking along Ramtund Peak and informed authorities late Monday afternoon. According to preliminary information, the group allegedly comprised three Pakistani and one local terrorist.Additional personnel from the Army, CRPF and police, along with reinforcements, were rushed to the area from Udhampur on Tuesday morning, officials said, adding that no contact was established with the suspects until evening.Ramtund area lies near the Seoj Dhar belt, situated on the Doda-Udhampur axis, which further connects to Kathua region. Terrorists have traditionally used this route to travel and hide, as the topography features dense vegetation and natural caves, officials said.The searches in Doda came four days after local police put up posters across J&K, announcing Rs 15 lakh reward for credible information leading to the arrest of self-styled Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat.Separately, security forces launched an intensive combing operation in Poonch’s Mendhar sector upon noticing suspicious movement near an under-construction tunnel. “A security guard manning the site spotted the suspects and fired three to four rounds as a precautionary measure, following which a joint team of SOG and CRPF launched a search operation around 6am Tuesday in the nearby forested stretches of Bhatadurian, Sangiot and adjoining areas,” an official said.
Article Summary: Cordon-and-search operations were initiated in Doda’s upper reaches after some locals captured a video of four suspected ultras trekking along Ramtund Peak. According to preliminary information, the group allegedly comprised three Pakistani and one local terrorist. The searches came four days after local police put up posters across J&K, announcing Rs 15 lakh reward.

Article Title: MP Parimal Nathwani urges Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren to resolve students' demands through dialogue following lathi charge
Article Text:
Parimal Nathwani urged CM Soren to have talks with students

NEW DELHI: A day after the student protestors were lathi-charged in Jharkhand during the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march, Independent MP Parimal Nathwurged Chief Minister Hemant Soren to sympathetically address student protests over alleged JPSC and JSSC irregularities, emphasising that constructive dialogue is the best path to a resolution.Taking to X, Nathwani posted, "Earnestly request Hon'ble CM Shri Hemant Soren and the Jharkhand government to sympathetically consider the demands of the students. I strongly believe that a peaceful resolution through dialogue is the best way forward to protect the aspirations of our young candidates."The ongoing agitation has largely centred on demands raised by aspirants of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC). Protesters have been demanding cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.Speaking to ANI outside Parliament, Nathwani earlier elaborated on the situation, noting that the state administration has already agreed to a significant portion of the protesters' grievances."The state government has already met about 80% of their demands. The CM should have looked into the remaining key issues," he said.Pushing for dialogue after the escalation of protests, he added, "As for the students, they went to the CM's residence and then to the Legislative Assembly; the lathi-charge that occurred was truly unfortunate. I would urge Hemant Soren to sit down with them immediately and find a way forward."Nathwani expressed solidarity with their youth's plight while cautioning against unrest. "Your issues are significant, and we stand with you regarding what you have endured, but a resolution will only come through dialogue," he stated.His remarks come after police resorted to a lathi charge on Monday evening to disperse students protesting outside the Jharkhand Assembly in Ranchi. Demonstrators vowed to continue their agitation over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations and demanded a CBI probe.Authorities deployed tear gas shells, water cannons, and lathi charges as a large number of aspirants attempted to move toward the Assembly.Meanwhile, Jharkhand Minister Deepika Pandey Singh earlier said the government had been engaging with the protesters and maintained that the administration had been instructed to maintain law and order."In a democracy, there is permission for protests; people are free to hold them. The administration is taking the necessary actions to maintain law and order. There will be no use of pellet guns, tear gas, or lathi-charge here," she said.On allegations of a communication gap, the minister said, "It wasn't a lack of communication; we held discussions for hours--talks have been ongoing for four days. We agreed to everything that was within the state government's capacity to address."She said cancellation of the CGL examination involved legal considerations. "The issue they are adamant about cancelling the CGL exam- involves judicial directives. The students should understand that the state government must operate within the framework of constitutional rights and established guidelines. We have accepted nearly every point," Pandey Singh added.She said the government was open to investigations into alleged financial irregularities."We have kept the investigation open-ended; the state government is ready to have the probe conducted under judicial monitoring. We have even invited the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to investigate the allegations of financial misappropriation," she said.
Article Summary: Parimal Nathwani urges Chief Minister Hemant Soren to sympathetically address student protests over alleged JPSC and JSSC irregularities. Protesters have been demanding cancellation of the J SSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.

'No connection at all with Tahir'

NEW DELHI: Two men sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) official Ankit Sharma during the 2020 North East Delhi riots have challenged their conviction and sentence before the higher court.The convicts, Nazim and Kasim, were among five people convicted by the Karkardooma court in Delhi in the murder case. The court convicted them and three others, including former MCD councillor Tahir Hussain, on July 13 and sentenced them to life imprisonment on July 31.Speaking to ANI earlier, Mohammad Asif, the brother of convicts Nazim and Kasim, claimed that his brothers had been falsely implicated in the case and denied any connection with Tahir Hussain."We will appeal in the High Court. One of my brothers, the younger one, Kasim, lived in the village. The other one too had gone to the village two days before the incident. His body was later recovered from a drain in the Dayal Pur area.

Article Title: No Chinese encroachment in Arunachal, social media claims 'attention-seeking ploy': Report
Article Text:
No 'slow encroachment' by China in Arunachal, report suggests, adding that the Army and ITBP are geared up to monitor and check Chinese activities along the border.

NEW DELHI: There is no “slow encroachment” by China into Arunachal Pradesh, new agency ANI reported citing sources on Tuesday. The sources also rejected claims circulating on social media, describing them as “attention-seeking ploys” that lack specific evidence."There is no slow encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh by China as alleged," they said."Due to undemarcated border at times the patrols face off each other, this is resolved through existing mechanisms and protocols in vogue. The Army and ITBP are geared up to dominate the border, monitor and check Chinese activities. Sensational claims like this without going into specifics are attention-seeking ploys," the report said citing sources.They said China has historically laid claim to Arunachal Pradesh, referring to it as “South Tibet”. During the 1960 border talks, Beijing had claimed around 69,000 sq km of territory in the state.Also read | 'Arunachal is integral part of India, nothing can change this,' says MEA on China's fresh 'objections' ⁠"China has claims on Arunachal as South Tibet, articulated in 1960 border talks, wherein they claimed approx 69,000 sq km of the state territory. ⁠In 1959 China attacked the Assam Rifles outpost at Longju and captured it.The area has since been in adverse possession and is frequently in news due to infra development done in this area by China," they said."During 1962 India-China War, major Chinese operations were launched in Kameng, Subansiri, Siyom, Siang and Lohit valleys. However, after ceasefire the PLA went back North of the LAC. Arunachal Pradesh shares a large border with Tibet along Great Himalayan range. Concerted infra push in recent years has enabled enhanced ptlg and surveillance of the area," they added.The report comes after the ministry of external affairs (MEA) reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is an "inalienable and integral part of India", referring to the recent "objection" by China over renaming places in the state."Let me reiterate this once again that Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable and integral part of India and this is a fact that is self-evident. At the same time, let me also underline that nothing can change this indisputable reality," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.India officially identified 27 locations in Arunachal by their standard names on the survey of India map, countering China's repeated attempts to assign Chinese names to places in the state.
Article Summary: There is no “slow encroachment” by China into Arunachal Pradesh, new agency ANI reported citing sources on Tuesday. The sources also rejected claims circulating on social media, describing them as “attention-seeking ploys” that lack specific evidence.

NEW DELHI: Pune Police on Tuesday registered an FIR against an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder from the United Kingdom for allegedly attempting to convert people to Christianity through religious gatherings.DCP Prashant Amrutkar of the Pune City Police's Special Branch said the accused, a Manchester resident, has been booked under relevant provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, and the newly enacted Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act, 2026.According to police, OCI cardholders are permitted to attend prayer meetings and participate in religious functions, but cannot preach or deliver religious speeches without the required permission.Police alleged that the accused spoke about following the path of Jesus and made statements about Hindu temples and deities that they claimed could create misconceptions, news agency ANI reports.The police suspect that the statements were made with the intention of misleading people and inducing them to embrace Christianity. Further investigation is underway.In a separate case, Pune City Police arrested a 21-year-old man under the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act, 2026 and the POCSO Act for allegedly attempting to convert and sexually harassing a minor girl, news agency ANI reported.The case was registered at Fursungi Police Station on August 5, and the investigation is underway.Police said it is the first case registered in Maharashtra under the newly enacted Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act, 2026.The developments come amid a wider debate over religious conversion and foreign funding. Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis on Monday said organisations that operate transparently and comply with the law have nothing to fear from the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026.Fadnavis also rejected the suggestion that the FCRA legislation targets any particular community. “This is not an issue concerning any one particular community. FCRA is not meant only for Christian organisations. It is applicable to all organisations, irrespective of which community they belong to,” he said.
Article Summary: UK-based OCI cardholder booked by Pune Police in alleged religious conversion case. Police alleged that the accused spoke about following the path of Jesus. Article Title: 'Bitter disdain persists': BJP slams Shashi Tharoor over Vande Mataram remark

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Tuesday slammed Congress leader Shashi Tharoor for claiming that standing through the full rendition of Vande Mataram pushes the limits of human endurance. BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan said that Tharoor's remark was at odds with the sacrifices of the freedom fighters who gave their lives for the country's independence while uttering "Vande Mataram.""Senior Congress leader states that the full original rendition of Vande Mataram, which takes 3 minutes and 10 seconds, is too lengthy for people to stand through respectfully and patiently," Kesavan said in a social media post on X."Is this not extremely ironic coming from the servile Congress party, which for more than 75 long years has patiently and sycophantically been kowtowing to the Nehru-Gandhi first family. Such callous remarks deeply dishonour and disrespect the selfless sacrifices of generations of freedom fighters who patriotically gave up their lives uttering "Vande Mataram" for our nation's independence," he added.Kesavan also accused Congress of showing disdain towards the song, claiming that the hesitance stems from appeasement politics and discomfort with traditional national symbols."From Nehru's Congress which truncated Vande Mataram to Rahul Gandhi, bitter disdain and antipathy of the Congress party against Vande Mataram persists. In a letter dated June 21, 1948, to Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee, Jawaharlal Nehru with his Macaulay colonial mindset said Vande Mataram's tune was not suitable for foreign orchestra and bands. Nehru demeaned Vande Mataram stating it was unfit to be our National Anthem," the BJP spokesperson said."We are truly thankful to PM @narendramodi ji for restoring the respect and honour of Vande Mataram and making sure it is rendered in its glorious original form at public events - and for the first time ever at the Red Fort this Independence Day. PM Modi ji has ensured a fitting tribute to the generations of brave heroes and heroines who selflessly sacrificed for our nation's freedom," he added.Earlier in the day, Tharoor questioned the practical implications of the Vande Mataram amendment, saying the requirement to sing the National Song in full at official functions could result in audiences standing for several minutes before and after events.In a post on X, Tharoor said the President had assented to the amendment, which was passed in Parliament without discussion. He said the amended provision requires the full National Song to be sung at the beginning and end of official functions, in addition to the National Anthem."The President has assented to the #VandeMataram Amendment, passed without discussion in Parliament, which requires the singing of the National Song in full at the start and ending of any official function, in addition to the National Anthem."As one who greatly respects both, and can sing the first two stanzas of the former (but not the other four, which were never required till now) as well as the entire anthem, i would like to point to just one practical consideration our zealots appear to have overlooked: human nature," Tharoor added."'Jana Gana Mana' requires audiences to stand respectfully and focus their attention for a reasonable 52 seconds. The National Song in full takes 3 minutes and 10 seconds. Tamil Nadu has just decided that both will be preceded by the State Song in Tamil for another 2 minutes. Do we really expect audiences to stand still and respectfully for six minutes before and after every function, a total of 12 extra minutes? Can respect and patience be legislated? I fear that the intent of the Bill, to promote greater respect for the National Song, will not be achieved, but its opposite may well be," he further said.President Droupadi Murmu had given her assent to the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, extending statutory protection under the law to the national song Vande Mataram.The national song Vande Mataram will be sung during the Independence Day celebrations at the iconic Red Fort on August 15.The Union government announced on Monday that this year's celebrations will focus on the contribution of India's youth towards achieving the goal of a developed nation, or 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047.

Referring to the reported use of force, he questioned how the Modi government responds to young people demanding answers about their future.He wrote in his post on X: "Pellet guns, Nail-studded lathis, tear gas fired at students who were peacefully asking questions about their own future. NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sam Pitroda on Monday backed protesting students in Jharkhand as an agitation over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations intensified in Ranchi. Criticising the government’s use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons, Pitroda called for “reform, accountability and compassion” as the protests entered their 18th day.The development comes as the Jharkhand students’ 'Vidhan Sabha gherao' march in Ranchi on Monday saw police use lathis and water cannons to disperse protesters. The march was organised over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).The protesters are demanding, among other measures, the cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.In a series of posts on X, the Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) global chairman said the grievances of young people should be addressed through dialogue."The images from Ranchi disturb me deeply”, he wrote.Pitroda said students should not be met with force, calling them India's future and expressing solidarity with Jharkhand's youth.In another post, Pitroda said, "Democracy requires governments to create space for peaceful dissent, dialogue and resolution."Pitroda's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students, urging the Jharkhand government to address their grievances. The Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand government is run by a JMM-led coalition in which the Congress is a partner.Pitroda also said the protesting youth deserved to be heard respectfully and urged authorities to address their concerns over fair examinations, transparent recruitment, employment opportunities and their prospects for the future."These are not unreasonable demands. India owes its youth a system they can trust”, he added in the postHe further said the concerns of students needed to be viewed in the context of the sacrifices made by their families."Behind every protesting student is a family that has sacrificed - often for years for education and the hope of a job.Pitroda criticised the JMM-led Jharkhand government over the handling of recruitment and examination-related grievances, saying delays in recruitment and failures in examinations risk eroding young people's trust in the system. He called for "reform, accountability and compassion" in addressing their concerns.Calling India's youth its "greatest assets", Pitroda said the country's demographic dividend could turn into frustration if education does not translate into opportunities and examinations fail to inspire confidence."We must redesign education, assessment and employment systems for this generation — not punish them for demanding change," he said.On Monday, police and protesters clashed during the march outside the Jharkhand Assembly. Police resorted to at least three rounds of lathicharge, while tear gas shells and water cannons were also used to disperse demonstrators.Injured protester alleged that police began the lathicharge without warning.The police have, however, given a different account of the events. Ranchi deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said a stone was thrown at a police jawan and alleged that some "anti-social elements" attempted to provoke police and officials during the protest.Addressing a press conference, Bhajantri said the police had exercised restraint throughout the demonstration and used "mild force" only after a situation arose in which a jawan's life was allegedly at risk.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said most students were peaceful but alleged that a section of protesters damaged barricades and pelted stones.The protest also affected Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi after taking part in the march.Mahto had been on hunger strike for nine days at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium before joining the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march despite his deteriorating health. He was later admitted to hospital.The police action drew criticism from political leaders across party lines. On Monday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students."The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong. Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X, on Monday.He further urged the Jharkhand government to address the students' grievances."The Jharkhand government must continue to hear these students out and resolve their issues immediately," he added.The JPSC and JSSC examinations have been at the centre of protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities. Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has registered an Enforcement Case Information Report under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.
Article Summary: Congress leader Sam Pitroda criticises government's use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons as protests enter 18th day. Protesters are demanding cancellation of JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action.

NEW DELHIi: Supreme Court on Monday admitted a petition challenging acquittal of Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim , who is serving a 20-year sentence for sexually assaulting two female disciples, in the 2002 murder of Sirsa-based journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana overruled protests by Rahim’s counsel R Basant that it was a case of acquittal and that the state had not filed any appeal against the acquittal.“This matter requires consideration. It is a reversal of conviction (recorded by the trial court). It is not an acquittal affirmed by HC. We are equally conscious that the state (CBI) will not appeal against the acquittal,” it said. The trial court had convicted Rahim and sentenced him to life imprisonment in Jan 2019.Admitting a petition by Arindam Chhatrapati, the complainant and son of the murdered journalist, the bench requisitioned the trial court records, including witness statements, for scrutiny. It posted final hearing of the matter in Nov last week.Basant said HC had recorded a categorical finding that the key witness could not be believed at all.“We will examine the special circumstances attending to the examination of the key witness and whether the appreciation of his evidence is appropriate,” responded the bench.The appellant said, “Despite affirming the categorical findings of the trial court on the existence of a conspiracy for the commission of Chhatrapati’s murder and upholding the convictions of the three co-accused under Section 120-B IPC read with Section 302 IPC, HC incorrectly arrived at a conclusion that participation of Baba Gurmeet Singh in the conspiracy is not proved.”Finding lapses in the local police probe, Punjab and Haryana HC had in Nov 2003, almost a year after the murder, transferred the investigations to the CBI. The key witness, referred to by the SC, is the ex-driver of Rahim.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Monday admitted a petition challenging acquittal of Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim. Rahim is serving a 20-year sentence for sexually assaulting two female disciples. The trial court had convicted Rahim and sentenced him to life imprisonment in Jan 2019.
