Now that the Home Minister is ready to answer every point in detail, he must not run away," Rijiju said.Rijiju’s remarks came amid an ongoing confrontation between the government and the Opposition over the recent student protests and police action against demonstrators. The issue has led to repeated disruptions in Parliament, with the Opposition demanding answers from the government and Rahul Gandhi seeking a response from Shah.The government has now agreed to a debate on the issue, with Shah expected to respond to the concerns raised by the Opposition.
Article Summary: NDA MPs greet PM Modi with Tricolour and slogans of ‘Vande Mataram’ and ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju criticised Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, saying he should not ‘run away’ from Parliament.

Article Title: IndiGo flight makes emergency landing after engine failure; full emergency declared at Chennai airport
Article Text:
IndiGo flight operating from Kolkata to Chennai with 224 people on board, declared a full emergency at 11.29pm.





CHENNAI: A full emergency was declared at Chennai airport late Tuesday night after an IndiGo flight from Kolkata developed a left-engine failure shortly before landing.IndiGo flight 6E-723, operating from Kolkata to Chennai with 224 people on board, declared a full emergency at 11.29 pm on August 11, according to Airports Authority of India (AAI) officials.Also read: 'High' PIC was standing, leaning behind: Inside the cockpit of Air India Delhi-Phuket flight The aircraft was scheduled to arrive at 11.30 pm, but the pilot noticed that the left engine had failed as he prepared to land. He alerted air traffic control, following which airport authorities activated emergency response measures to facilitate the aircraft's safe landing.The aircraft landed safely on Runway 25 at 11.37 pm with all 224 people on board.The full emergency was withdrawn at 11.47 pm. Airport authorities said all operations remained normal following the incident.
Article Summary: IndiGo flight 6E-723, operating from Kolkata to Chennai with 224 people on board, declared a full emergency at 11.29pm. Pilot noticed that the left engine had failed as he prepared to land. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 25 at 11:37pm.

Article Title: ‘Raped, whipped, 20 knife wounds’: Teen keeps Nagpur girl under ‘digital arrest’ for 3 months before assault
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





NAGPUR: The 19-year-old Thane youth accused of raping and trying to kill a 16-year-old girl in Nagpur allegedly kept her under “digital arrest” for nearly three months, using mobile phone access, threats and constant video calls to control her, police said Tuesday.The girl was held hostage at a rented flat, raped repeatedly, whipped with a leather belt and inflicted with 20 knife wounds.She was rescued on Aug 3 from the flat in Nagpur’s Dighori area after her parents filed a missing complaint. The youth is currently in jail in Nagpur.Investigators traced a strap and a belt allegedly used in the assaults to two pet shops in Nagpur. “The neck strap and belt were designed to keep dogs on a leash. We question the shop owners and staff,” a police officer said.Police said the accused used “digital arrest” to force the girl to follow his instructions after meeting her on Instagram. About two months ago, he allegedly told the girl to go to the terrace of her flat and start a video call.He also ordered her to sleep under her bed. When she hesitated, he allegedly threatened to circulate her objectionable photographs on social media. Fearing the consequences, she complied, police said.
Article Summary: The girl was held hostage at a rented flat, raped repeatedly, whipped with a leather belt and inflicted with 20 knife wounds. She was rescued on Aug 3 from the flat in Nagpur’s Dighori area after her parents filed a missing complaint. Police said the accused used “digital arrest” to force the girl to follow his instructions after meeting her on Instagram.

Article Title: ​​Youths on indefinite hunger strike against CJP founder shifted to hospital
Article Text:
The two youths have accused CJP leadership of favouritism and excluding grassroots members from the newly constituted core committee





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Two youths, Manish Brahmabhatt and Rahul Pandya, who had been on an indefinite hunger strike in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to protest the list of core committee members announced by Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) on Aug 6, were admitted to a hospital on Monday after alleged detorioration in their health condition.The two youths have accused CJP leadership of favouritism and excluding grassroots members from the newly constituted core committee. Speaking to the media, Brahmabhatt alleged that the police forcibly shifted them to the hospital. He, however, said the agitation would continue despite their hospitalisation.Following the duo’s hospitalisation, two new volunteers replaced them at the protest site, announcing that they would carry forward the hunger strike against CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.Brahmabhatt and Pandya had earlier said they stood shoulder to shoulder with Dipke during the Jantar Mantar agitation in Delhi, but only people close to Dipke were invited to the core committee meeting. The duo claimed that the movement belonged to youth from across the country and not to any individual, demanding greater internal democracy within the organisation. They also sought representation for volunteers from every state in the committee.Dipke did not issue any response to the hospitalisation of the two protesters till Monday evening.
Article Summary: Manish Brahmabhatt and Rahul Pandya had been on an indefinite hunger strike in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to protest the list of core committee members announced by Cockroach Janta Party. The two youths have accused CJP leadership of favouritism and excluding grassroots members from the newly constituted core committee.

Article Title: Putin's vacation home exposed to attack, missile launch pad guarding Putin's Palace blazing for three hours after drone strike: Report
Article Text:
Putin's Palace (Credit: east2west news)

What is inside Putin's vacation home?

The vacation home of Russian President Vladimir Putin was exposed to a drone attack after a missile launch pad that used to guard one of Putin's lavish vacation homes was set ablaze, the Telegraph reported. The missile launch pad is around 12 miles from Putin's Italianate palace complex near Gelendzhik, southern Russia. Major Robert Brovdi, the commander of Ukraine's unmanned systems forces, claimed that the launchpad was ablaze and sputtering for three hours.Ukrainian media claimed that the S-400 air-defense system that guarded the residence fired six missiles before getting damaged. Satellite images taken after the strike showed at least one launcher was destroyed, Brovdi said.On August 7, Ukrainian forces disabled a nearby electronic-warfare station known as Volna Kupol Garant, which had been jamming Starlink satellite communications within a roughly 20-kilometer radius around the residence, a Moscow Times report said. Military analyst Yan Matveev told The Moscow Times that knocking out the large, easily recognizable station opened the way for the attack on the S-400; the station had been effective against drones.Not much is known about the vacation home, but The Telegraph reported, based on claims, that the luxurious complex housed a casino, vineyard, spa, ice rink, theatre, pole-dancing room, hookah lounge, “aquatic disco”, miniature railway room and more. In 2023, it was reported that a chapel had been added.Putin rarely visits the Black Sea vacation home and prefers his highly fortified luxury dacha on Lake Valdai, 185 miles east of Moscow. This residence is believed to be home to Alina Kabaeva, his secret long-term partner, and their two sons. It is protected by at least 27 towers mounted with Pantsir anti-aircraft systems, costing some £16m per unit.Ukraine’s military intelligence said on Monday that Kyiv’s drones had also struck two Russian S-400 Triumf air defence launchers, as well as an antenna it uses to control medium-altitude Orion drones in occupied Crimea. Losses from the strike could amount to the equivalent of tens of millions of dollars, Ukraine’s directorate of intelligence said.
Article Summary: missile launch pad is around 12 miles from Putin's Italianate palace complex near Gelendzhik, southern Russia. Ukrainian forces disabled a nearby electronic- warfare station known as Volna Kupol Garant, which had been jamming satellite communications within a roughly 20-kilometer radius around the residence.

Article Title: 'Premeditated and gruesome assault': Delhi high court denies bail to Olympic medallist Sushil Kumar in murder case
Article Text:
Sushil Kumar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Delhi high court has refused to grant bail to Olympic wrestler Sushil Kumar in the alleged murder of former junior national wrestling champion Sagar Dhankar.Justice Purushaindra Kumar dismissed Kumar's bail plea on August 6, citing concerns about his ability to influence witnesses, his conduct before his arrest, the seriousness of the alleged offence and his ability to affect the outcome of the ongoing trial.The judge noted that while bail is generally the rule and jail the exception, the case involved a "premeditated and gruesome assault resulting in death". The court said this was supported by the recovery of a firearm, video evidence and other material that is yet to be examined during the trial.Kumar's counsel sought bail on the ground that circumstances had changed since his earlier bail was cancelled. The lawyer pointed out that Ashok Dhankad, Sagar's father whose complaint had led to the earlier cancellation of bail, had not supported the prosecution's case during the trial.The defence also argued that Kumar had already spent more than five years in custody and that only formal and official witnesses remained to be examined.Delhi Police and Dhankar's father opposed the bail plea.The high court, however, said the defence's claim that Sagar's father had not supported the prosecution was disputed. It also referred to the Supreme Court's earlier decision cancelling Kumar's bail, in which it had noted his social standing and influence and the fact that witnesses had turned hostile whenever he was given temporary liberty."Whether the deposition of Ashok Dhankad (deceased's father) does or does not support the prosecution is, moreover, a matter of appreciation of evidence that must await the outcome by the trial court. It cannot be treated as a change in circumstances sufficient to unlock the door that the Supreme Court closed," the court said."In these circumstances, this court is not persuaded that the petitioner has made out a case either for a genuine change in circumstances within the meaning of the liberty reserved by the Supreme Court, or, independently, for the grant of regular bail," it concluded.Kumar was arrested in May 2021. A sessions court later granted him one week's interim bail for knee surgery on July 19, 2023.The Supreme Court cancelled his bail on August 13, 2025, setting aside a Delhi high court order. It said Kumar's "domineering influence" over witnesses and the possibility of delaying the trial proceedings could not be ruled out.The High Court had granted Kumar bail on March 4, 2025. Earlier, on February 6, a trial court had rejected his bail plea, saying the possibility that he could influence witnesses "cannot be ruled out".In October 2022, the trial court framed charges against Kumar under Indian Penal Code provisions relating to murder, criminal conspiracy, intimidation and rioting with a deadly weapon. Charges were also framed under the Arms Act.The trial court had said Dhankar was abducted and taken to the stadium, where he was severely assaulted by several accused persons using baseball and hockey sticks.
Article Summary: Olympic wrestler Sushil Kumar is accused of murdering Sagar Dhankar. The Delhi high court has refused to grant bail to Kumar in the alleged murder. Justice Purushaindra Kumar dismissed Kumar's bail plea. He cited concerns about his ability to influence witnesses.

Article Title: NEET hunger strike continues, Cauvery water row intensifies, Vijay moves delimitation resolution: What is trending in Chennai today
Article Text:
Chennai faces significant political and public focus on three key issues

The anti-NEET protest refuses to die down

Cauvery dispute back to center stage

Delimitation on Vijay





CHENNAI: The political and public agenda in Chennai today is dominated by three big issues – the ongoing anti-NEET stir, the fresh Cauvery water dispute and the political debate on delimitation.The Tamil Nadu Assembly has already passed a resolution seeking abolition of NEET for undergraduate medical admissions, but the anti-NEET protesters on hunger strike in the city say their agitation will continue.The Cauvery issue has simultaneously resurfaced in the wake of the Cauvery Water Management Authority directing Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs or one TMC of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from August 12.Meanwhile, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam leader and CM Vijay is expected to bring a resolution against delimitation in the Tamil Nadu Assembly, adding yet another political flashpoint.And Chennai is witnessing an odd cocktail of student politics, inter-state water issues and electoral politics.The anti-NEET protesters continued their hunger strike in Chennai, demanding that the government respond to their demand to abolish the medical entrance examination.The agitation comes in the wake of the Tamil Nadu Assembly passing a resolution to urge the Center to amend relevant laws and do away with NEET as a requirement for undergraduate medical admissions.That the protest has continued suggests that the issue remains politically and emotionally live in Tamil Nadu.The Cauvery Water Management Authority’s order to Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of Cauvery water daily for 15 days has brought back a familiar interstate dispute.The order is on the basis of differences over earlier instructions and the demand for adequate water supplies by Tamil Nadu. The issue is likely to remain politically sensitive as both states balance agricultural requirements, reservoir levels, and competing claims.CM Vijay is also likely to move a resolution against delimitation in the Assembly. The move brings his fledgling political outfit straight into one of the big constitutional and electoral debates in Tamil Nadu.With the NEET issue, Cauvery issue and delimitation issue all simmering at the same time, Chennai’s political temperature is set to rise thru the day.
Article Summary: Chennai faces significant political and public focus on three key issues. Tamil Nadu Assembly has already passed a resolution seeking abolition of NEET for undergraduate medical admissions. Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam leader and CM Vijay is expected to bring a resolution against delimitation.

Article Title: Nolan Wells update: ‘Violent’ history of accused threat maker revealed in new investigation
Article Text:
Nolan Wells update: ‘Violent’ history of accused threat maker revealed in new investigation

Edward James Porter’s past includes arrests, gun threats and court cases

Nolan Wells death case: What the new Edward James Porter details show

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Berwyn, Illinois, man accused of threatening people connected to the investigation into Nolan Wells’ death has a long record of arrests involving violence, theft and violations of court orders, according to records reviewed by investigators. Edward James Porter, 33, is now facing a federal charge after allegedly threatening to kill witnesses and their relatives. He is also accused of making a separate threat to cut up a witness and put the remains in a suitcase. Porter is being held in federal custody as questions remain over Wells’ death and has drawn fresh attention nationwide.Porter’s criminal history dates back to 2011, with records showing about two dozen arrests. The cases included domestic violence, theft and breaking court orders of protection, according to records obtained by NBC 5 Investigates.Police also dealt with Porter over a firearm threat involving an ex-girlfriend. He had an Illinois Firearm Owner’s Identification card and a handgun. Police said he threatened her, telling her, “I’m going to shoot you…” The charges were later dropped after the woman did not continue with the case.Records do not show whether Porter got the gun or FOID card back.His record also includes several later arrests involving allegations of gun violence, assault and threats. Many of those cases were eventually dropped because victims did not testify. That history is now being examined as Porter faces a federal case tied to the Nolan Wells investigation.Wells, an 18-year-old from Mississippi, disappeared during a July 4 boat trip to Horn Island with friends. His body was found in the water two days later. The circumstances of his death remain unresolved.An independent autopsy commissioned by his family found the cause and manner of death “undetermined pending investigation” and said foul play could not be ruled out. The official state autopsy results have not been publicly released.The threats involving Porter are separate from the question of who caused Wells’ death. Authorities have not accused Porter of killing Wells. Instead, federal prosecutors say Porter inserted himself into the investigation by contacting people connected to the case.Court records cited in the investigation say phone calls and internet records linked the threats to Porter and the Berwyn apartment where he was living. He allegedly threatened to kill a witness, the witness’s family and any police officers who responded.In another alleged threat, he said he was going to cut up a witness and put the remains “into a suitcase.”Porter was arrested in Berwyn after federal agents, accompanied by local police, took him into custody. NBC 5 Investigates reported that he did not resist. He is being held by federal authorities and is due in court in Gulfport, Mississippi, on Sept. 2.For now, the Wells investigation and the federal case against Porter remain separate legal matters. The new records add more detail about the man accused of making threats, but they do not answer the central question surrounding Nolan Wells’ death.
Article Summary: Edward James Porter, 33, is now facing a federal charge after allegedly threatening to kill witnesses and their relatives. He is also accused of making a separate threat to cut up a witness and put the remains in a suitcase. Porter’s criminal history dates back to 2011, with records showing about two dozen arrests.

Article Title: These cattle were left to survive alone on an Alaskan island; generations later, their DNA was unlike most US breeds
Article Text:
Image: The Livestock Conservancy

How cattle ended up isolated on a remote island in the Gulf of Alaska

Genome-wide testing revealed a rare mixture of Yakut and Hereford ancestry

Harsh island conditions may have reshaped the cattle’s genetic architecture

Why the Chirikof cattle became important to conservation scientists

A wildlife refuge faced a difficult decision over the feral herd

More than abandoned cattle, the herd became a record of evolution

For generations, cattle have roamed Chirikof Island, a remote island in the western Gulf of Alaska where human management became almost irrelevant to their survival. Cut off from the mainland and living in a harsh environment, the animals persisted as a feral population while generations of domesticated cattle elsewhere were shaped by deliberate breeding.A 2016 study published in Heredity, ‘ Origins of cattle on Chirikof Island, Alaska, elucidated from genome-wide SNP genotypes ,’ by J. E. Decker, J. F. Taylor, J. Kantanen, A. Millbrooke, R. D. Schnabel, L. J. Alexander and M. D. MacNeil used genome-wide genetic data to investigate where these unusual cattle came from and how distinct they had become. The researchers found that the herd was not simply an abandoned American breed. Instead, it carried a distinctive mixture of Siberian Yakut and British, particularly Hereford, ancestry, with genetic evidence suggesting that life on Chirikof Island had further influenced the population.Chirikof Island lies about 61 kilometres from the nearest land and roughly 74 kilometres southwest of the Kodiak Archipelago. Its lack of a deepwater harbour made movement to and from the island difficult, meaning that relatively small groups of cattle could become isolated there.The cattle's history reaches back to the period of Russian colonial rule in Alaska. The researchers note that Yakut cattle from Siberia were likely introduced first, with cattle from Yakutia being brought to settlements in Russian America during the late 18th and 19th centuries.The genetic evidence indicates that these Yakut-related animals eventually formed part of the ancestry of the Chirikof herd. Later, European cattle were introduced, adding another layer to the population's history.Historical records indicate that cattle originating from the United States reached Chirikof Island by the mid-1880s. By 1927, a count recorded approximately 400 beef cattle on the island. Additional cattle, including Herefords and potentially other breeds, were reportedly introduced during the 20th century.The result was not a single conventional breed, but a genetically mixed population developing in unusual isolation.To understand exactly what had happened to the island herd, Decker and his colleagues analysed DNA from 10 Chirikof Island cattle and compared their genetic profiles with cattle from around the world.The researchers examined more than 43,000 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) across the cattle genomes. They then compared the island animals with 137 breeds and populations using several population-genetic methods. The results revealed a striking pattern.The Chirikof cattle fell genetically between Hereford and Yakut cattle, consistent with substantial ancestry from both. Their analyses estimated approximately 49-59% Hereford-like ancestry and 33-40% Yakut-like ancestry, with the remainder coming from other cattle populations.Another analysis estimated that about 34.4% of their ancestry came from a Yakut ancestor, with the rest being most similar to Hereford.The genetic results also matched the historical timeline. The researchers inferred that Yakut-related cattle arrived first, European taurine cattle were introduced approximately 120 years before the study, and a later wave of Hereford cattle arrived around 40 years before the study. This combination made the Chirikof herd unusual among North American cattle.The most intriguing part of the study was not simply discovering where the cattle came from. It was finding evidence that life on Chirikof Island may have changed the genetic composition of the herd.The animals had been living unmanaged in an isolated and relatively harsh environment for many generations. Natural selection therefore had an opportunity to favour genetic variants that helped some individuals survive and reproduce under those conditions.The researchers identified 12 SNPs across eight loci showing patterns consistent with strong selection. The analysis was considered underpowered because of the small sample size, so the authors treated these findings cautiously. Nevertheless, genes near the identified regions were associated with functions including immune defence, embryonic development and cancer.The findings suggest that the island cattle were not merely a frozen remnant of the breeds originally introduced there. They had been changing.The discovery had implications beyond the history of one isolated herd. Feral livestock can retain genetic variation that is rare or absent from intensively managed commercial breeds. Because domesticated animals are often subjected to strong selective breeding for traits such as growth, milk production or meat quality, unusual populations can preserve genetic variants that have disappeared elsewhere.The Chirikof cattle appeared particularly interesting because their mixed ancestry and long isolation had produced a population that was genetically distinctive compared with other North American cattle.The researchers concluded that the population appeared to be at least as distinct as recognised cattle breeds and that its combination of British and Siberian ancestry was unique among the North American breeds included in their comparisons. They also suggested that the animals could contain variants associated with adaptation to the island's demanding environment. That made the herd potentially valuable as a source of genetic diversity.There was an important conservation conflict surrounding the cattle.Chirikof Island became part of the Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge in 1980, and the US Fish and Wildlife Service sought to reduce the impact of introduced animals on island ecosystems. The final grazing lease for Chirikof expired in 2000, while a permit to remove the cattle expired in 2003. The cattle nevertheless remained on the island.Wildlife managers wanted the cattle removed because grazing could damage habitat, particularly habitat important to birds. Their removal, however, could also lead to the disappearance of a genetically unusual cattle population.That created a complicated conservation question: should the animals be treated simply as an introduced species damaging a wildlife refuge, or should their unusual genetic characteristics also be considered?The researchers argued that understanding the herd's genetic diversity could provide an objective basis for making that decision.The story of the Chirikof cattle is ultimately about what can happen when domesticated animals are removed from the systems that normally control their breeding.Their ancestors arrived through human migration and livestock introductions. But once the animals became isolated on Chirikof Island, their evolutionary trajectory was no longer entirely directed by people.Yakut and Hereford ancestry became intertwined. Geographic isolation limited further immigration. Generations passed under the demanding conditions of an Alaskan island. And natural selection appears to have left its own mark on the population.Decker and his colleagues' study therefore revealed something more complicated than a herd of feral cattle. It uncovered a genetically distinctive population carrying a record of Russian, British and American livestock history, and potentially, the genetic signatures of adaptation to one of Alaska's most isolated environments.
Article Summary: Genome-wide testing revealed a rare mixture of Yakut and Hereford ancestry. Harsh island conditions may have reshaped the cattle’s genetic architecture. The findings suggest that the island cattle were not a frozen remnant of the breeds originally introduced there.

Article Title: Indian student charged for killing 81-year-old man in Florida after driving Cadillac like a bullet at 100mph, attorney asks court to allow him to return to Columbia University
Article Text:
indian student Akash Das was arrested and charged with vehicular homicide (Photo: WPBF)

Attorney says Das is from a good family

Eyewitnesses said Das was driving like a bullet

Indian student Akash Das was behind the wheel when his Cadillac SUV collided with an Audi sedan, and the 81-year-old driver of the Audi, Gary Neal Fields, died. The accident took place in July, and Das was arrested in August and his bail was set. The police arrest report was recently made public and it revealed that four vehicles were involved in the fatal crash and Das was speeding at 100 mph in a 45 mph zone.Investigators who analyzed the data from the Cadillac's airbag control said Das showed "willful and wanton disregard for the safety of others". Das made his first court appearance on August 6. Palm Beach Post reported that he remained in custody as of the morning of August 7. Circuit Judge Donald Hafele set Das' bail at $125,000 and ordered that he be placed on in-house arrest upon his release.Defense attorney Adam Farkas, who represented Das in court, said Das is currently living in South Florida to complete an internship with a company that specializes in AI. He said that Das is seeking to return to New York to finish his pursuit of a Master's degree from Columbia University.Farkas did not respond to the speeding allegation, but said there was no evidence that Das' actions were intentional.The attorney also said that Das is from a good family and has no police record. "He's charged with negligent vehicular homicide, meaning that there was no intent at all," Farkas said. "He comes from a very good family, he's never been in trouble before and hopefully we can put this all behind him. It was a tragic accident that occurred."Das' Cadillac crashed into the right rear door of Fields' Audi, causing the Audi to crash into a Nissan SUV that was sitting at a stop sign. The Nissan then collided with a Volvo SUV that was traveling west on Victoria Falls. Fields was unresponsive and when he was taken to Palm Beach Gardens Medical Center, he died. Das and the Nissan's driver had injuries that were not life-threatening. The Volvo driver was not hurt.One driver told investigators the vehicle came up behind her “like a bullet,” shaking her car as it sped past. Another witness recalled thinking, “They’re going to kill someone,” moments before the collision. Das remains charged with vehicular homicide.
Article Summary: Indian student Akash Das was behind the wheel when his Cadillac SUV collided with an Audi sedan, and the 81-year-old driver of the Audi, Gary Neal Fields, died. The police arrest report was recently made public and it revealed that four vehicles were involved in the fatal crash and Das was speeding at 100 mph in a 45 mph zone.

Article Title: Indian expat from Kerala killed in Dubai gas cylinder blast; colleague recalls moments before explosion
Article Text:
Shijin Paul/Image: X

Colleague recounts fire before blast

Explosion struck during firefighting efforts

An Indian-origin man from Kerala was killed in a gas cylinder explosion at a car showroom on Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai on Monday, the Indian Consulate in Dubai confirmed, Gulf News reported.The victim was identified as Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district.A relative told the outlet that Shijin succumbed to his injuries at a hospital after the explosion."I was informed by his company about the blast. Unfortunately, he had passed away by the time I reached the hospital," the relative said.Shijin worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. According to his family, he had joined the company in November. He is survived by his parents and wife.A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises."Some of us, including Shijin and I, went out of our showroom after some of our colleagues alerted us about a fire," Abid, a photographer who worked with Shijin, told the newspaper."There were people from several shops nearby too, not just from our showroom.Many people came running after spotting the fire."Abid said the flames appeared to have broken out near a gate close to neighbouring auto service workshops."There is a gate in one corner of the showroom, and the fire started somewhere there. There are some auto service companies next to our showroom, and the fire was near their location."According to Abid, people at the scene attempted to contain the fire with extinguishers before the cylinder exploded."People were trying to put out the fire with fire extinguishers. The explosion occurred while efforts were underway to douse the fire. Everyone ran away," he said.He added that he did not immediately realise Shijin had been caught in the blast."I don't know who all got hit. I got to know about his death later," Abid said.The Indian Consulate said it remains in contact with Shijin's family and the authorities to provide support following the incident.
Article Summary: Shijin Paul, 27, from Kottarakkara in Kerala's Kollam district, died in the blast. He worked as the showroom's multimedia marketing specialist, handling social media and videography. A co-worker who witnessed the incident said employees rushed outside after colleagues noticed a fire on the premises.

Article Title: Delhi Mosque Demolition: Delhi Demolition Drive Near Faiz-e-Elahi Mosque: Police Clash During MCD Action
Article Text:
Delhi demolition drive: MCD carries out action near Faiz-e-Elahi mosque following HC order; 5 cops injured in stone pelting

Delhi: 5 Cops Injured, 10 Detained As Anti-Encroachment Drive Near Mosque Turns Violent

Demolition drive at Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque near Turkman Gate in Delhi on Wednesday. Image Credit: Tarun Rawat/TNN







NEW DELHI: Multiple police personnel were injured during a demolition drive in central Delhi early on Wednesday after locals and miscreants attacked them with stones.The police is trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting and will initiate strict action against them.Delhi Police have registered an FIR against unknown persons and around 10 people have been detained for questioning so far, officials said.Police are scanning CCTV footage, ground visuals and body-camera recordings to identify those involved in the attack on the police team.While the FIR has been lodged against unidentified persons, investigators said four to five suspects have already been identified and further legal action will follow.Special commissioner (Law and Order) Ravindra Yadav said that the action started around 1 am."MCD conducted demolition as per the high court's orders on the encroached land. Stones were pelted at the police at night. We used minimal force to push back."DCP (Central) Nidhin Valsan said, "The action is still ongoing. We deployed our staff for security. 4 to 5 officers suffered minor injuries. As soon as we get the CCTV camera footage, ground footage, and body camera footage, we will identify the miscreants and take legal action."The demolition was carried out by the MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area. The drive kicked off around 1 am, with around 17 bulldozers pressed into service.The action followed an order of the Delhi High Court, which declared a dispensary and a community hall adjoining the mosque illegal and directed their removal.The administration appealed to local residents to maintain peace.Anticipating major disruptions, the Delhi Traffic Police also issued a traffic advisory, warning of congestion on several key roads on Wednesday. Traffic around Ramlila Maidan and adjoining areas is expected to remain affected through the day.
Article Summary: 5 cops injured in stone pelting during demolition drive in central Delhi. Police are trying to identify the miscreants who engaged in stone-pelting. The demolition was carried out by MCD to remove illegal constructions around the Faiz-e-Ilahi Mosque in the Turkman Gate area.

Article Title: Laxmi Nagar assault: New clip shows SUV crashing into house; accused Omkar Yadav claims self-defence in viral video
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Another CCTV clip related to the Laxmi Nagar assault has surfaced, showing a group of men arriving first, opening a gate and assaulting a man. Moments later, a Thar SUV was seen speeding towards the house and crashing into the wall, after which several men got out of it and the assault continued. Meanwhile, accused Omkar Yadav has released a video on social media defending his brother, gym caretaker and key accused Satish Yadav alias Pintu Yadav.A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault recently when the man was beaten up, his wife was said to be molested, and their son was stripped and assaulted on the street.The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business, leading to the dispute. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage-related issue, Yadav, along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son, a senior officer said.An earlier CCTV footage had shown the couple's son being dragged onto the road, stripped and beaten up by a group of four-five men. The presence of police personnel in parts of the footage also raised questions. Police claimed the assault stopped after they arrived while the victims alleged that they were beaten up in full view of the cops, a claim that is being verified.According to the complaint, the couple's son came out after hearing the commotion and was assaulted. The couple also said their two sons had left the house following the attack.Police said main accused Yadav was arrested while the other accused were absconding. Omkar, one of the absconding accused, posted a video on social media, saying his brother had been working with the complainant for "20-25 years" and was running the gym for the past "12-13 years". He questioned why objections over the gym were raised only in the past five-six months. "If we captured the land, why did she start complaining only now?" he asked.Omkar further alleged that the legal proceedings were "one-sided" and claimed that he was also being targeted. He identified himself as a worker of a party and alleged that he was being defamed by an opposition party.Referring to the incident, Omkar said, "On Jan 2, I got a call from my brother. I reached the spot after 10-15 minutes. If I am seen kicking two or three times in the video, it was in self-defence. They started hitting first."A case has been registered at the Laxmi Nagar police station under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint, criminal trespass, assault or use of criminal force to outrage the modesty of a woman, acts intended to insult a woman's modesty and criminal intimidation.
Article Summary: A dispute over a gym operating from a residential property in east Delhi's Laxmi Nagar allegedly escalated into the assault. The man runs a gym from the basement of his house and caretaker Yadav allegedly cheated him and attempted to take over the business. On Jan 2, during an argument over a basement- and sewage- related issue, Yadav along with his associates, assaulted the couple and their son.

Article Title: Heavy rain, Kanwar rush wreak havoc on traffic; Yamuna sludge linked to ammonia spikes, cybercrime crackdown: Delhi news today
Article Text:
Rain, diversions and huge numbers of pilgrims have caused traffic disruption in several areas of the capital, according to reports.





NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for yet another weather-dominated day with concerns about traffic, pollution and public safety with heavy rains and continued Kanwar rush posing a tough combination for commuters. Rain, diversions and huge numbers of pilgrims have caused traffic disruption in several areas of the capital, according to reports.Meanwhile, a new study has put the spotlight on the Yamuna , noting that sludge in the river may be behind periodic ammonia spikes that affect the capital’s water treatment system.The city’s pollution-control expenditure is also in focus after the Delhi Assembly was informed that hundreds of crores collected as pollution cess remained unspent. In the policing arena, Delhi Police busted a cybercrime network and arrested nine people, while another high-profile road-safety case involving a speeding BMW has renewed concerns about reckless driving.Kanwar movement, rain put pressure on trafficThe capital is facing major traffic problems as five days of Kanwar related movement coupled with rain have created major traffic problems here. Slow movement is being witnessed on several stretches due to traffic diversions and religious processions intersecting already congested roads.It's especially hard at rush hour.For people in Delhi, the disruption is about more than longer journeys. Rain quickly reveals poor drainage, and diversions push more traffic onto neighboring roads. With preparations for Independence Day in full swing, traffic management is turning out to be a major concern for the city.Yamuna sludge raises water quality concernsA study by the Central Pollution Control Board has suggested that sludge in the Yamuna may be one of the causes of spikes in ammonia in the river. The problem of high ammonia levels has plagued Delhi’s water treatment plants several times, forcing authorities to change operations when the quality of raw water falls.The finding adds a new dimension to the long-standing problem of Yamuna pollution. The sludge that has accumulated is also a cause of the problem, but the main worry remains sewage discharge and industrial pollution, which require a more comprehensive clean-up strategy.Internet-crime crackdownThe Delhi Police has also stepped up its action against organized cybercrime and arrested nine persons in a recent operation. The arrests highlight the growing prevalence of digital scams targeting residents, especially the elderly.Meanwhile, a fatal collision involving a speeding BMW has put reckless driving back in the spotlight. Together the developments tell a story of a Delhi grappling with traffic management, environmental pressures and urban crime at the same time.
Article Summary: Rain, diversions and huge numbers of pilgrims have caused traffic disruption in several areas of the capital. A new study has put the spotlight on the Yamuna, noting that sludge in the river may be behind periodic ammonia spikes. Delhi Police busted a cybercrime network and arrested nine people.

Article Title: Want to work for CJP? Party invites volunteers for tech team; check roles on offer
Article Text:
The recruitment post said the team is working on building "real tools for a real movement" and called for volunteers willing to contribute to the initiative.

CJP expands organisational structure

CJP backs Jharkhand student protesters





NEW DELHI: Technology lead of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Rohan Deshpande, has invited volunteers to join the party's technology team and work on its website.In a post shared on X, Rohan announced openings for multiple technical roles and said the positions are unpaid.He also urged applicants to apply only if they can dedicate a "decent" amount of time to volunteering.According to the recruitment poster, the CJP Technology team is looking for volunteers for four roles — Backend Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Frontend Engineer and Security Engineer.The party has listed seven openings in total, with two positions each for Backend Engineer, DevOps Engineer and Frontend Engineer, and one position for a Security Engineer.The recruitment post said the team is working on building "real tools for a real movement" and called for volunteers willing to contribute to the initiative.Interested applicants have been asked to fill out an online form shared by the party. The application form is available at the CJP volunteer recruitment form.The volunteer recruitment comes after the CJP recently announced its National Working Committee as part of efforts to strengthen its organisational framework.Rohan has been named the party's Technology Lead. Founder Abhijeet Dipke has been appointed National Convener, while chief spokesperson Saurav Das and spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka have been named Co-Conveners.The newly formed committee will oversee the party's expansion plans, including setting up state coordination committees, Lok Sabha-level units and city-level teams across the country over the next six months, according to the CJP.Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has condemned the alleged police lathi-charge on student protesters in Jharkhand and expressed solidarity with student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who is undergoing treatment in hospital.According to a CJP statement, Dipke spoke to Mahto over a video call while the student leader was hospitalised. The outfit claimed Mahto had been on a nine-day hunger strike before the police action and that his condition deteriorated following the alleged lathi-charge.The CJP claimed Mahto was placed on oxygen support after developing severe chest pain and sustaining multiple injuries during the police action. It alleged that the police crackdown targeted students taking part in a peaceful protest.During the video call, Mahto reportedly recounted the police action and circumstances leading to his hospitalisation, the statement said."Whether it is Jantar Mantar in New Delhi or the streets of Jharkhand, such severe police brutality against peaceful student demonstrators is cruel, inhuman, and entirely unacceptable," Dipke said.He also expressed support for Mahto, calling him a "true hero" for his efforts on behalf of the student community and saying that the CJP stood firmly with his struggle.
Article Summary: The party has listed seven openings in total, with two positions each for Backend Engineer, DevOps Engineer and Frontend Engineer. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has condemned the alleged police lathi-charge on student protesters in Jharkhand.

Article Title: Independence Day 2026: Delhi Police tightens security, over 1,600 personnel deployed in South zone
Article Text:
Ahead of Independence day Police personnel across districts have been deployed on the streets





NEW DELHI: With Independence Day celebrations just days away, Delhi Police has intensified security across the national capital, deploying additional personnel, setting up checkpoints and pickets, and increasing patrolling, vehicle checks and drone surveillance to prevent any untoward incident on August 15.Police personnel across districts have been deployed on the streets, with heightened focus on suspicious persons and vehicles, criminal elements and sensitive locations. Additional pickets and checkpoints have also been established at several places.Delhi Police DCP South Anant Mittal said officers of all ranks were on the ground as part of the heightened security arrangements.Pickets have been established at various locations in South Delhi, where police are checking suspicious individuals and vehicles."Officers of all ranks are out on the ground patrolling, given the heightened sensitivity surrounding August 15th," Mittal said, adding that the checking operation was being carried out with a strong focus on security ahead of Independence Day.Joint Commissioner of Police, Southern Range, Vijay Kumar said more than 1,600 police personnel, including women personnel, have been deployed in the southern zone. Around 60 pickets, including border, major and minor pickets, have been set up in the area.He said integrated checking was being carried out at major pickets, with traffic police working alongside PCR and local police personnel. Four-wheelers and two-wheelers are being checked, along with parking areas."The main focus is on the criminal elements, the bad characters. We do check them; we check abundant vehicles and parking areas," Kumar added.The security arrangements also include intensified patrolling and inspections by senior police officers. Joint Commissioner of Police Madhur Verma said Station House Officers and senior officers would patrol their respective areas and conduct inspections, while picket checks had been intensified."Comprehensive security arrangements have been put in place. We have a multi-layered security system," Verma said.In East Delhi, DCP Rajeev Kumar said all officers and personnel were on the streets as part of the Independence Day security preparations.Intensive checking is being carried out, and action is being taken against anti-social elements, he said.Police are also using drones for surveillance, particularly to maintain an aerial watch over areas where large gatherings or increased movement are expected.The intensified security comes as Delhi prepares for Independence Day celebrations, when several parts of the capital witness increased movement of people, vehicles and security personnel.Police have consequently increased ground-level surveillance and checking to detect suspicious activity at an early stage.The multi-layered arrangements involve local police, traffic personnel and other security teams working together at checkpoints and sensitive locations.Border areas and major entry and exit points are also being closely monitored as part of the security exercise.With August 15 approaching, Delhi Police officials said the focus would remain on preventive security, regular patrolling and quick action against any suspicious activity to ensure peaceful Independence Day celebrations across the capital. (ANI)(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi Police has intensified security ahead of Independence Day celebrations. Police personnel across districts have been deployed on the streets. Additional pickets and checkpoints have also been established at several places. Police are also using drones for surveillance, particularly to maintain an aerial watch over areas.

Article Title: Girls not safe even at home: Delhi court on man who raped 12-year-old cousin
Article Text:
Judge Mishra asked Delhi Legal Services Authority (north-west) to provide Rs 15 lakh to the survivor.(AI image)





NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has sentenced a man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on his 12-year-old cousin, terming his act “highly abominable”.Girls aren’t safe even within the “four walls” of their own homes when persons like the convict show no respect for the pious relationship between a brother and sister, Judge Niti Suri Mishra said.She condemned convict Ajay’s actions as “heinous, inhumane and insensitive behaviour towards minor children who are the epitome of innocence.”During the sentencing, the court highlighted the impact of such crimes on a child’s mind, observing how “the dastardly memories of the offence may haunt the child, having negative impacts on her mental health for life.”Though the defence had prayed for leniency, submitting that the convict, now 42, had three children and aged parents dependent on him, the court rejected the plea. No circumstances concerning the accused could outweigh the immense mental health issues, including low self-esteem and psychological distress, that a child might undergo because of such an incident, the judge said.The incident doesn’t remain an isolated event in a victim’s life, she said.It has “serious ramifications on the reputation of the victim’s family in society.” Families are subjected to “boundless embarrassment and abasement” for no fault of their own, the judge remarked.The case goes back to 2013. Prosecutor Yogita Kaushik Dahiya said that when the child was alone at home while her siblings were playing outside and her parents were away, Ajay — then 25 — who was the son of the victim’s paternal aunt, arrived at their residence and committed penetrative sexual assault against her.Judge Mishra asked Delhi Legal Services Authority (north-west) to provide Rs 15 lakh to the survivor. “Not only such children, but even their families face humiliation, pain and trauma. Hence, it’s the entire family of the victim that suffers,” she added.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has sentenced a man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on his 12-year-old cousin. Judge Niti Suri Mishra condemned convict Ajay’s actions as “heinous, inhumane and insensitive behaviour towards minor children’
